correctness.rationale: A mixed-radix diagonal one-parameter subgroup has pairwise distinct ambient tensor-coordinate weights, so its projective fixed locus consists exactly of coordinate tensor lines. Every such line has multilinear rank \((1,\ldots,1)\), hence lies in every positive subspace variety, and there are no further fixed points. Compactly supported Euler characteristic localizes to the fixed locus for algebraic \(\mathbb C^*\)-actions; the package includes a Rosenlicht-stratification proof that does not assume smoothness. Thus every cumulative subspace variety has Euler characteristic \(\prod_i a_i\). Exact flattening-rank loci form a finite constructible stratification, and induction on the product rank poset forces every higher exact stratum to have compactly supported Euler characteristic zero. The checker independently replays weight separation and finite poset subtraction across a broad family.

value.rationale: Multilinear rank is one of the basic intrinsic rank notions for higher-order tensors and underlies Tucker decomposition and dimensionality reduction. Subspace varieties vary substantially with the bound vector in dimension, degree, singularities, and equations, yet the theorem shows that ordinary Euler characteristic is constant across the entire positive multirank filtration. The exact-stratum consequence is stronger: every genuinely higher multilinear-rank layer has compactly supported Euler characteristic zero. This gives a complete all-format topological classification for a central tensor-rank hierarchy and precisely identifies a natural invariant that cannot detect higher Tucker rank.
